cases.name: Agentic AI dropshipping exactly as the video shows it
cases.model: Agentic AI dropshipping exactly as the video shows it: StoreBuild and Zendrop template Shopify store with about 10 preset products, China-shipped by default, AI static image ads on Facebook, Claude as ad researcher and store manager.
cases.one_line: Cheap, fast setup and a strong Claude fit, but unproven, and China shipping breaks this week's test; use its workflow now and hold China-shipped products as a later fallback.
how_it_works_steps: Open a new Shopify store through the StoreBuild funnel. A theme and 10 preset Zendrop products load in the first 8 minutes of the video. Store build is $0. Shopify is $1 a month at first (verify at signup). Zendrop is $29 a month once products are linked (01_video_decode.md, sections 1, 2a, 2b).

Claude as store manager audits the store and rewrites product descriptions, FAQ and SEO text through the Shopify connector. Dhruv approves each write. Theme text and reviews stay manual (01_video_decode.md, minute 33 to 37).
Claude as ad researcher pulls competitor static ads from an ad library and writes image prompts. An image tool turns the supplier photo into static ads. The video stops here.

Dhruv adds what the video leaves out: Shopify Payments verification, a new Meta ad account, pixel and purchase event, one broad sales campaign, and a delivery window stated by the buy button (01_video_decode.md, section 5).

A customer pays on Shopify. Zendrop charges Dhruv's card when the order is fulfilled. China stock ships in 1 to 5 business days and takes 10 to 15 business days in transit (03_fulfillment_and_money.md, sections 2a and 3e).
Shopify Payments pays out later. First payout for a new store is about 7 to 14 days (ESTIMATED, 03_fulfillment_and_money.md, finding 1). Refunds come out of his balance after that.
cases.days_to_first_sale: About 2 to 6 days from today. This range is ASSUMED. The store itself can be ready in a day. The video covers no payment setup, ad account, pixel or campaign, so ads go live later than the store. In the transparent creator tests that got a sale, the first sale came 20 minutes to about 24 hours after ads started (02_youtube_sweep.md, section 4.3, self-reported). Some products got no sale at all: two of three in the Tilbury test had no day-1 sales. Main risk to the range: a new Meta ad account has a Meta-set daily limit, and static-only ads plus an 11 to 20 business-day delivery line may slow the first sale. The size of that effect is UNKNOWN.
cases.cash_needed_to_start: $500 to $1,000, which is Dhruv's cap. The model fits inside it, but not together with a $2,000 sales week. What it buys: Shopify at $1 a month to start (verify at signup). Zendrop at $29 a month for 1 to 20 linked products (Shopify App Store listing, VERIFIED, 01_video_decode.md section 2b). The video calls Zendrop free; it is not. Store build $0 (storebuild.ai FAQ, VERIFIED). One sample unit, cost UNKNOWN because the Zendrop catalog is behind a login. The rest is ads. The creator's own minimum test is $25 a day per ad set, 3 ad sets, at least 7 days, about $525 by plain multiplication (01_video_decode.md section 5, not script-checked). AdLibrary.io at $29 a month after a 3-day trial is not needed. On top of this, each order is paid to the supplier before Shopify pays out. Supplier float for $2,000 of sales is $600 to $1,200 at ASSUMED cost shares (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 2c).
cases.profit_per_order: For this exact model: UNKNOWN. The video shows no price, product cost, shipping cost, ad cost or order. The demo dog dryer's cost and price are "not available" (01_video_decode.md section 7). Closest script evidence is the China-shipped comparison in ranked.md, at the tough ad cost with a 10% refund allowance (ASSUMED): knife set +$1.85 per order (US stock +$0.21), mattress vacuum -$8.29, galaxy projector -$26.69. So one of three is barely above zero. Across all 16 scouted products, 0 pass the cushion rule and 0 still earn money if cost is 20% higher and refunds are 10% (ranked.md). Creator tests with stated costs end near break-even: +$52 on $57 of ads, likely $54.01 on $249.66 of ads over 25 sales (caption unclear, UNKNOWN until checked), about $85 profit on a $1,000 sales day (02_youtube_sweep.md sections 2.2, 2.3, 6.2, all self-reported). All files are in /home/user/commerce-os/research/fast-test-2026-11-21/.
cases.week1_sales_realistic: $0 to about $600. This range is ASSUMED. Reasoning: the repo's reality check puts a first test under $1,000 at low hundreds to about $1,200 of revenue, with a small loss to a small profit (battle_brief.md, 04_reality_and_benchmarks.md finding 9, ESTIMATED). The ranked.md first-week table (US stock, tough ad cost, no payout yet) shows $500 covers 4 to 6 orders and $1,000 covers 9 to 13 orders, and every line ends in a loss after setup and sample. No script run exists for a China-shipped first week. I place this model in the lower part of that range for three reasons. No transparent test won on AI static ads alone (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.5). An 11 to 20 business-day delivery line in the Christmas gift window should hurt conversion, size UNKNOWN. Black Friday week CPMs run 16 to 84% above September (battle_brief.md). The $2,000 stretch target is not realistic for this model: ranked.md puts the cash needed for $2,000 of sales at $1,925.83 or more even on US stock.
cases.inventory_needed_up_front: None. No stock is bought. Each order is paid to Zendrop when it is fulfilled, before Shopify pays out (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 2). Dhruv orders one sample unit to himself the same day. From China it arrives after about 11 to 20 business days, so the first weeks of sales would run without him having seen the product (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 7, point 5).
cases.delivery_time_to_customer: China stock on Zendrop, the model's default: 1 to 5 business days processing plus 10 to 15 business days transit. Most orders arrive 11 to 20 business days after ordering (Zendrop help articles, VERIFIED vendor claim, 03_fulfillment_and_money.md sections 1a and 3e). Orders placed after about Nov 25 to Dec 9 miss Christmas on those numbers (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 6b, script output). The video itself states no delivery time. For contrast, Zendrop US stock is 4 to 8 business days, up to 10 in Q4.
strongest_evidence: Setup is cheap and fast, and that part is verified. Store build is $0 with no sales commission (storebuild.ai FAQ). A theme and 10 products load inside the first 8 minutes of the video (captions). Zendrop is $29 a month for 1 to 20 linked products (Shopify App Store). Source: 01_video_decode.md sections 1, 2a, 2b.

Claude's two roles work on camera and match tools Dhruv already has. Shown in more than one video: rewriting titles, descriptions, FAQ and SEO text through the Shopify connector with approval, summarizing competitor ads, writing image prompts (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.7, VERIFIED as shown). Zendrop has an MCP server for product search, import, orders, tracking and fulfillment with confirmation (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 1a, VERIFIED). The creator's prompt document says "Do not invent reviews" and "Stop for approval before modifying Shopify" (01_video_decode.md section 2f).

Parts of the method match what credible creators do. Tilbury's expert ran 3 products at once on $300 so one flop would not end the test. Fogarty: "let's launch all of the products". Creators imply 2 to 4 product tests before a winner. Robinson tests 5 to 10 statics at $50 a day and reads them after $150 to $160. Source: 02_youtube_sweep.md sections 2.2, 2.7, 2.11, 4.4 (self-reported, ESTIMATED).

China cost is lower where a price was found. Knife set $20.89 China against $26.49 US. Galaxy projector $15.45 against $28.06. Source: ranked.md, China-shipped comparison (card prices, ESTIMATED). The gain is small after a 10% refund allowance (ASSUMED): the knife set's tough-case profit moves from $0.21 to $1.85.

The repo's own research names when China-shipped is acceptable, which supports a later fallback role: own store only, a product with no US stock, outside the Christmas window, an 11 to 20 business-day window stated on the page and at checkout, and a per-product check of the real transit time. Source: 03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 7.
honest_weaknesses: There is no proof this model makes money. The video launches no ad, takes no order and shows no cost, result or delivery time (VERIFIED from captions). The $4.2M belongs to a stocked golf brand that ships from North Carolina in 2 to 3 days and reported about 10% net profit in September 2026 (self-reported). The creator earns from the Shopify referral, Zendrop, his ad-spy tool and a $97 a month club. He tells viewers to use a US warehouse. Source: 01_video_decode.md sections 0, 3, 4.

China shipping fails this week's test. Delivery is 11 to 20 business days. Orders after about Nov 25 to Dec 9 miss Christmas. The same-day sample arrives after the first weeks of sales. Slow delivery feeds refunds, Shopify reserve risk and Meta's customer experience score, on a profile tied to Dhruv's client ad work. China parcels now carry duty (ESTIMATED). Direct-from-China parcels are also on CLAUDE.md's out-of-scope list, so this needs Dhruv's explicit exception. Source: 03_fulfillment_and_money.md sections 3b, 6b, 7.

It does not meet "every order makes money". 0 of 16 scouted products pass the cushion rule. The best China-shipped case is +$1.85 per order at the tough ad cost and the other two are negative. Every first-week line in ranked.md ends in a loss. No transparent creator test shows every order profitable in week 1 (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.3). A $500 to $1,000 test also never leaves Meta's learning phase (ranked.md: $1,961.50 of ad spend for pets, $2,430.50 for home).

AI static ads alone have not carried a transparent test. Sales in those tests came from video. Fogarty's student got no add to carts from image ads on product 1. Robinson says his first AI batch's messaging was "horrible". The video's "three times cheaper" claim has no data. Copying a named competitor's ad look, and his September advice to strip AI metadata, break repo rules and put the ad account at risk. Do not copy those steps. Source: 02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.5; 01_video_decode.md section 5.

The template store is generic. StoreBuild claims over 1.5 million stores, and every user in a niche reportedly gets the same ten products (ESTIMATED, a competitor's review). Generic stores with slow delivery score 1.4 to 3.3 on Trustpilot and Amazon undercuts them (battle_brief.md). Ten products split a small budget too thin to read; Wold says testing ten "would just be gambling". The demo product is a mains-powered dog dryer with UNKNOWN cost, certification and ship-from, and it touches Dhruv's safety exclusion. Claude could not edit theme text, and no agent ran ads to a profit without a person.
cases.path_to_10k_month: A product from the catalog must win on ads, then move to US stock with far more profit per order than ranked.md shows today ($0.21 to $1.85 in the tough case). For scale, Barkfare's math needs about 295 orders a month. Unproven here.
cases.automation_fit: Claude can do: competitor ad research, image prompts, static ads, product copy, FAQ, SEO, daily order and ad summaries, Zendrop order and tracking checks. Manual: theme text, reviews, Meta account and pixel setup, approving every write and fulfillment, refunds, checking images match the shipped item.

cases.name: Fast lane: one-product store, US-stock supplier, Meta ads
cases.model: Fast lane: one-product store, US-stock supplier, Meta ads
cases.one_line: The only lane that can show real sales within days for under $1,000, but its best products only break even after ads, so run it as a capped test.
how_it_works_steps: Today: pick one product from the two green rows in ranked.md (knife set at $99.00 or rechargeable wall sconce pair at $109.99). Order one unit to Dhruv's home. Open Shopify, Shopify Payments and a new Meta ad account so their waiting clocks start.

Before any ad money: Dhruv reads the real unit cost, stock count and ship time in a logged-in US-stock catalog. Rerun scripts/fast_test_rank.py on that cost. Go only if profit at the tough ad cost is not negative. If neither product holds, stop. Zero winners is an allowed result.

Claude drafts a one-product page in store/: pair or pack pricing, a ship-from-US line with the supplier's stated days, a guarantee, FAQ, an honest new-brand tone and no fake reviews. Dhruv applies it by hand.

One broad Meta campaign, built paused, published by Dhruv. Small daily cap through Cyber Monday (Nov 30), main budget after, because the ad price premium fell to about 20% two days after Cyber Monday (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 6a, ESTIMATED). A fixed loss cap and the CLAUDE.md section 4 kill rules replace 'every order profitable' for this test.

Each order: the customer pays on Shopify, Dhruv pays the supplier the same day, the supplier ships from US stock, tracking goes to the customer. When the sample lands, real photos and a demo video replace the first images.
Shopify pays out about 7 to 14 days after the first sales (ESTIMATED, 03_fulfillment_and_money.md finding 1). Then decide on the data: stop, test the second product, or move a winner toward stock.
cases.days_to_first_sale: About 3 to 7 days from today if the cost check holds. Build time of 2 to 5 days at 1 to 3 hours a day is ASSUMED. After ads go live, the first sale came in 20 minutes to about 24 hours in the creator tests that got one (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.3, ESTIMATED, self-reported). Main reason for the spread: theme edits are done by hand and the new Shopify and Meta accounts have their own checks. Two of seven transparent tests failed outright (04_reality_and_benchmarks.md section 2.9), so "never" is a real outcome.
cases.cash_needed_to_start: $500 to $1,000, Dhruv's own cap. Script output in ranked.json: $42.49 (knife set) to $52.69 (sconce pair) covers Shopify at $1 (ESTIMATED), a domain at $15 (ASSUMED) and one sample unit. The rest floats ads plus supplier cost at $89.68 to $99.88 per order before any Shopify payout. That covers 4 to 5 orders on $500 and 9 to 10 orders on $1,000 (ranked.md). Not in those figures: product liability insurance (cost UNKNOWN), a supplier app such as Zendrop at $29 a month (03_fulfillment_and_money.md finding 3), and any paid creator video.
cases.profit_per_order: ranked.md and ranked.json (scripts/fast_test_rank.py; costs ESTIMATED from marketplace cards, 6% refunds ASSUMED). Knife set at $99.00: +$14.79 at the established-brand ad cost of $48.61, +$0.21 at the new-store ad cost of $63.19, -$5.09 if cost is 20% higher. Sconce pair at $109.99: +$14.60, +$0.02, -$7.32. At 10% refunds and the new-store ad cost both lose money: -$3.75 and -$4.38. None of the 16 products passes the cushion rule. Honest reading: break-even per order, not profit, until Dhruv's real ad cost is measured.
cases.week1_sales_realistic: First 7 days: $0 to about $440 (rough ASSUMED: 0 to 4 orders, because ads start mid-week on a small daily cap in Black Friday week). Whole capped test: up to about $990. ranked.md: at the new-store ad cost, $1,000 covers 10 knife-set orders ($990.00) or 9 sconce orders ($989.91); $500 covers 5 ($495.00) or 4 ($439.96). The script's result after setup and sample is -$40.43 to -$52.62. 04_reality_and_benchmarks.md section 6.2 lists the common outcomes as "a few sales or none" or "a few hundred dollars to about $1,200". The $2,000 goal needs 19 to 21 orders and $1,925.83 to $1,950.47 in cash, which is above the budget.
cases.inventory_needed_up_front: None. One sample unit to Dhruv on day one: $26.49 (knife set) or $36.69 (sconce pair), card prices, ESTIMATED (ranked.md). After that, each customer order is paid to the supplier when it is placed, before Shopify pays out (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 2).
cases.delivery_time_to_customer: 4 to 8 business days door to door from US stock, up to 10 in Q4 (Zendrop's own numbers, VERIFIED vendor claim, 03_fulfillment_and_money.md finding 4). The AliExpress US-stock cards say "Fastest delivery in 6 days", but the knife-set card shows no delivery days (candidates_home.md, ranked.json). No test order has been timed, so the real figure is UNKNOWN until the sample lands. A by-Christmas promise is safe for orders through about Dec 10 and arguable to Dec 14 (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 6b).
strongest_evidence: Speed: paid-traffic dropshipping is "the only model here that can produce a sale within days" and US stock is rated "best fit for speed with fewer refunds" (04_reality_and_benchmarks.md section 7). First sale came 20 minutes to about 24 hours after ads went live in the creator tests that got one (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.3, ESTIMATED).

Two products clear the new-store ad cost on US stock: knife set at $99.00 with $63.40 before ads, sconce pair at $109.99 with $63.21 before ads, against a tough ad cost of $63.19 and a benchmark of $48.61 (ranked.md). Both miss the cushion rule narrowly: target CAC of $47.55 and $47.41 against the $48.61 benchmark (ranked.json).

Proven demand with no single owner: 23,100 Amazon units a month across 79 knife-set listings and 20,950 across 56 sconce listings at $40 or more. Sconces have 22 brands and none above 2,000 a month (ranked.json, candidates_home.md, DataForSEO read 2026-11-21).

The loss is capped and small in the script's tough case. No stock is bought. Week 1 on $1,000 ends at -$40.43 (knife set) or -$52.53 (sconce pair) after setup and sample (ranked.md). The CLAUDE.md section 4 kill rules pause a test at half its budget if blended CAC is above break-even.

US stock is where the platform evidence points. Shopify lists extended delivery as a reserve trigger and Meta's buyer survey asks about shipping delays (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 7, VERIFIED). Stores stating US stock show oneisall 4.9, Haven 4.7 and Nood 4.0 on Trustpilot against Pillow Slides 1.6 and Galaxy Lamps 1.4, with Uproot an exception at 2.0 on 19 reviews (05_store_teardowns.md section 4). Meta's weapons ad policy bans "non-culinary knives/blades/spears", so kitchen knives are not named as banned (https://transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/restricted-goods-services/weapons-ammunitions-explosives, opened 2026-11-21).
honest_weaknesses: It does not meet "every order makes money" on the evidence. 0 of 16 products pass the cushion rule and 0 still earn money at a 20% higher cost with 10% refunds (ranked.md). The two best earn $0.21 and $0.02 an order at the new-store ad cost. No creator with a transparent cost sheet shows a first week where every order was profitable (02_youtube_sweep.md section 4.3).

The costs are one AliExpress US search-card price each, on listings with 12 sales, not supplier quotes. The $26.49 knife listing is a 15-piece block set of about 8 to 9 lb, not the 3-piece gift set the $99 offer describes. Sconce styles closer to Amazon best sellers cost $45.91 to $52.89, above the 20% stress case that already loses $7.32. Stock can run out mid-test. CJ and Zendrop prices are unread. Blind shipping and return terms are UNKNOWN (ranked.json, candidates_home.md).

It starts in the most expensive ad week of the year. Established brands paid 59% more per thousand impressions in Black Friday week than in September, and home and decor paid 116% more (Lebesgue, ESTIMATED, 03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 6a). Both green products are home products. A new ad account has a Meta-set daily limit, and the test never leaves the learning phase, which needs $2,430.50 of ad spend a week in home (ranked.md).

The $2,000 stretch goal is out of reach on this budget and a poor week is common. $2,000 needs $1,925.83 to $1,950.47 in cash (ranked.md). "A few sales or none; most of the ad money gone" is listed as a common outcome (04_reality_and_benchmarks.md section 6.2). With the kill rules, a bad test loses about half the ad money plus setup and sample, roughly $300 to $400 on the $1,000 plan (rough ASSUMED figure, from the script's ad spend of $568.74 to $631.93).

It sells before Dhruv has held the product, from a store with no reviews. Amazon sells the sconce pair at $45 to $57 against our $109.99 (ranked.json). Meta bars "reviews of ... bladed items" in ads (same Meta policy page), so review-style knife videos are out. "Japanese" and "Damascus" wording are legal traps, knives bring injury complaints, and insurance cost is UNKNOWN. A policy strike would touch the Facebook profile Dhruv uses for client work (03_fulfillment_and_money.md section 5).
cases.path_to_10k_month: Real ad cost must land near the $48.61 benchmark, not $63.19, and verified cost must hold. At $14.60 to $14.79 an order, $10,000 takes roughly 700 orders a month (rough ASSUMED). So a winner must move to bulk stock and bigger orders, as Barkfare's math shows.
cases.automation_fit: Claude drafts the product page, policies, FAQ, ad copy and images, builds the Meta campaign paused, reruns the money script and checks kill rules daily. Manual: Shopify signup and theme edits, account verification, publishing ads, paying the supplier per order, customer replies, filming the sample.

cases.name: Barkfare own brand (the slow lane)
cases.one_line: Barkfare cannot sell this week, but at bulk cost it keeps +$22.70 an order in the tough case (ESTIMATED) against $0.21 for the best fast-test product, so prepare it now.
how_it_works_steps: This week, $0: Dhruv pastes the 14 drafted supplier messages (about 15 minutes per /home/user/commerce-os/suppliers/SEND_LIST.md). Replies take 1 to 3 days. Claude scores the quotes and reruns the money math on real costs.
Dhruv orders 5 kits by express through escrow from the best low-minimum supplier. About $404 ESTIMATED (outputs.json, trial.cash_for_kits).
Kit 1 is the sample. Dhruv does the kneel test, fold check and car fit, and films it. The page and ads go live only if it passes.

Sell the other 4 kits at $149 with a small Meta test (about $154 of ads at the benchmark). Dhruv ships each by USPS from Florida. Expected result: 4 customers, real data and a small loss of about $103 (outputs.json).

After 10 happy customers: 150 kits by sea to a US 3PL (about $6,976 ESTIMATED). Scripted profit becomes +$34.25 per order, or +$47.37 on the $189 bundle. Note: 4 trial sales do not reach 10, so a second small batch is needed first.
Shopify Payments pays out to the DBA bank account. Add-ons and Amazon FBA come after the 3PL is running.
cases.days_to_first_sale: Rough ASSUMED: about 3 to 8 weeks after the supplier messages go out. No sale this week or next. Main reason: no kit exists yet and nothing has been sent. The fastest low-minimum suppliers are judged at 15 days to land 5 kits after ordering (/home/user/commerce-os/reports/ranked_suppliers_speed_2026-11-17.md, unverified). Made-to-order units were expected mid to late December on a Nov 17 start (/home/user/commerce-os/reports/final-plan-2026-11-17.md). The older plan with a separate sample step shows 30 days best and 58 typical (/home/user/commerce-os/research/sourcing-2026-11-15/plan.json). A sample must pass before any page or ad goes live.
cases.cash_needed_to_start: About $858 for the trial: $300 setup, 5 kits, and ads for 4 sales (/home/user/commerce-os/research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/rank_outputs.json, cash_needed). Kits alone about $404 and ads about $154 (/home/user/commerce-os/research/money-math-2026-11-19/outputs.json, trial). This fits his $500 to $1,000. All ESTIMATED: the per-kit cost is based on a 20-kit express batch and a 5-kit batch costs more (UNKNOWN until quotes). Product liability insurance cost is UNKNOWN (/home/user/commerce-os/reports/answers-2026-11-15.md). The step that actually makes money, 150 kits, needs about $6,976 more (outputs.json, goal.cash_for_first_bulk_order_150). The $1,800 budget does not cover that.
cases.profit_per_order: From /home/user/commerce-os/research/money-math-2026-11-19/outputs.json, per $149 order, ads at $38.51 (Meta pet median, ESTIMATED). 5-kit trial shipped from home: -$5.64 (tough case -$17.19). Same trial at 52.5% duty: -$13.55. Bulk 150 kits through a 3PL: +$34.25 (tough +$22.70), break-even ad cost $72.76, target $54.57, passes the cushion rule. $189 bundle at bulk: +$47.37 (tough +$35.81). Every cost is ESTIMATED; no supplier quote is VERIFIED. The brief's newer pet benchmark is $39.23, so these would come out slightly lower; the script has not been rerun. For comparison, /home/user/commerce-os/research/fast-test-2026-11-21/ranked.md shows 0 of 16 fast-test products passing the cushion rule.
cases.week1_sales_realistic: $0 this week and $0 next week. There is no kit on hand and no approved sample, so nothing can be sold honestly or within the FTC shipping rule. The $2,000 stretch goal is out of reach for this model. Even when the trial runs, it tops out at 4 sales and $596 of revenue (outputs.json, trial.revenue_if_all_sold), ending about $103 down at benchmark ads and about $150 down in the tough case. Its realistic week-1 output is not sales. It is sent messages and the first real quotes, at zero cash.
cases.inventory_needed_up_front: 5 kits, about $404 ESTIMATED. One is the sample, 4 are for sale. Later, 150 kits by sea, about $6,976 ESTIMATED (outputs.json). At the $10,000 goal, about $13,715 of stock per month of sales (outputs.json, goal.inventory_cash_for_one_month).
cases.delivery_time_to_customer: Trial: Dhruv ships each order by USPS from Florida. Days to the door are UNKNOWN until a test order. Bulk: a US 3PL ships each order. The house target is 2 to 8 business days (CLAUDE.md section 2), not yet confirmed. Nothing here is VERIFIED. Stock in the US is this model's delivery advantage once it exists.
strongest_evidence: Proven demand at a premium price from several sellers. RuffRover $159.95, Ruff Liners $169.99, 4Knines $169.99 list (checked Nov 15). About 5,500 units a month sell on Amazon at $130 or more (ESTIMATED). Source: /home/user/commerce-os/reports/full-synopsis-2026-11-19.md section 3 and /home/user/commerce-os/reports/holistic-analysis-2026-11-14.md.

The thickest scripted margin in this battle. At bulk cost the kit earns +$34.25 per order and +$22.70 in the tough case, and passes the cushion rule (target ad cost $54.57 against a $38.51 benchmark). Its $72.76 break-even ad cost sits above the $51.00 tough pet ad cost used in ranked.md. In ranked.md the best fast-test product earns $0.21 in the tough case and none of 16 pass the cushion rule. Sources: /home/user/commerce-os/research/money-math-2026-11-19/outputs.json and /home/user/commerce-os/research/fast-test-2026-11-21/ranked.md. Costs are ESTIMATED.
It ranked first of 24 options for a small start: score 72, next best 54. Source: /home/user/commerce-os/research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/rank_outputs.json.

The fast-test research itself points at this model. The video creator's real store is a stocked brand shipping from a North Carolina warehouse. The style reference store is a manufacturer brand shipping from the USA in 3 to 4 days. Winning stores use kit pricing, a guarantee line and add-ons. Source: /home/user/commerce-os/research/fast-test-2026-11-21/battle_brief.md.

The groundwork is done and the next step costs $0. Brand approved, offer stack and page mockups drafted, 14 supplier messages ready, low-minimum suppliers listed (minimum 2 to 5, ESTIMATED from listings), and two factories that customs records show supplying 4Knines and Ruff Liners. Source: /home/user/commerce-os/suppliers/SEND_LIST.md and /home/user/commerce-os/reports/decisions.md.

Monthly fee $0 (ESTIMATED, /home/user/commerce-os/data/channel_params.json). Creators post their own videos, so Dhruv stays off camera. Orders arrive in the shop. Dhruv ships by USPS. The parcel must be scanned within 2 business days and delivered within 6 (VERIFIED).

TikTok deducts its referral fee (6% on TikTok's own page, 8% reported by third parties, unresolved) and the creator commission from each sale. Payout is 31 days after delivery for a new shop. It drops to 8 days once the shop has a performance score, which needs 30 orders in 90 days (VERIFIED).

Optional and later: TikTok Shop ads (GMV Max) at about $50 a day minimum (ESTIMATED). Its return on spend is UNKNOWN in channel_params.json, so add it only after creator videos are already converting.

cases.name: Print-on-demand from US printers
cases.one_line: Lowest-cash, US-made, already-approved gift test that earns about $19 an order on repo math, but only if run now as a capped Christmas side lane with honest delivery dates.
how_it_works_steps: Day 1: Dhruv opens Shopify and a Printful account, connects them, and orders one sample bundle to his home. No supplier talks are needed. These are Dhruv's actions, not mine.

Claude drafts one product page in store/: custom dog portrait sherpa blanket plus 8x10 canvas at $149 under Barkfare, with a plain 'made to order' delivery line and a Christmas order cutoff date. Dhruv applies it.

A customer orders and uploads a dog photo. Claude makes the AI-illustrated portrait, Dhruv checks the likeness, and the customer approves a proof by email. The page labels the art as AI-made and never calls it hand-drawn.

The approved file goes to Printful through its Shopify app or API. Printful prints in 2 to 5 business days and ships from the US in 3 to 4 business days. Dhruv's card pays Printful for each order (product $51.57 plus shipping $21.18, data/economics_inputs.csv).

Meta ads are created paused with a hard cap of $150 to $350 and start only when Dhruv approves. Kill rule: stop any ad with no sale once it has spent $57.69, the break-even ad cost in data/economics_outputs.csv.
Shopify pays out 7 to 14 days after the first sale (battle_brief.md). Money kept is the payout minus Printful, card fees, refunds and ads.
cases.days_to_first_sale: About 4 to 10 days from today (ASSUMED). The store, page and Printful link can be ready in 2 to 3 days because no supplier approval or stock is needed. The main delay is Meta: a new ad account has a daily spend limit and business verification can take up to 14 business days (battle_brief.md). On Etsy alone the answer is UNKNOWN and probably slow: Printify says its sellers average 165 days to their first $1,000 (vendor figure, 04_reality_and_benchmarks.md line 397).
cases.cash_needed_to_start: About $210 to $430 before the first order (rough ASSUMED sum). Shopify about $1 a month for the first 3 months (CLAUDE.md, verify at signup). One sample bundle about $60 to $80 (reports/full-synopsis-2026-11-19.md section 11). Ads $150 (the plan Dhruv approved Nov 18) up to $350 (the capped plan size in ranked.md). Then float: each order costs $51.57 product plus $21.18 shipping paid to Printful (data/economics_inputs.csv) before Shopify's first payout in 7 to 14 days (battle_brief.md). It fits inside $500 to $1,000 with no stock at risk.
cases.profit_per_order: Custom dog portrait blanket plus canvas at $149 through Printful, from data/economics_outputs.csv (scripts/economics.py, run Nov 13): $57.69 left before ads. After ads: +$19.18 at the pet benchmark and +$7.63 in the tough case (benchmark x 1.3). High case +$45.84. Low case (10% discount, 10% refunds, paid retouch) loses $26.59. Caveats: that run used a $38.51 benchmark and a 3.9% fee. The brief's pet benchmark is $39.23 and Shopify is 2.9%. It was not rerun; the two changes roughly cancel (rough ASSUMED). The $149 price and the 5% refund rate are ASSUMED. For comparison, the best of the 16 dropship products in ranked.md earns $14.79 at benchmark and $0.21 in the tough case. Cheap print-on-demand items ($15 to $30 tees, mugs, ornaments) lose money on every Meta order (battle_brief.md), so this case rests on the one high-priced bundle only.
cases.week1_sales_realistic: 0 to about 7 orders, so $0 to about $1,000 (rough ASSUMED). Reasoning: ranked.md's capped plan gives 6.9 to 8.9 orders for a pets product on $350 of ads, at $51.00 to $39.23 per order. That benchmark is for established brands in normal weeks. Setup eats 2 to 4 days of the week, Black Friday CPMs run 16 to 84% above September (battle_brief.md), and nobody has proven the $149 price. With the approved $150 ad cap, expect 0 to 4 orders (rough ASSUMED). The $2,000 stretch needs about 14 orders at $149 (rough ASSUMED) and is unlikely. This lane should not carry that goal.
cases.inventory_needed_up_front: None. Every item is printed after the customer pays. The only purchase is one sample bundle to Dhruv's home, about $60 to $80 (reports/full-synopsis-2026-11-19.md section 11). A failed design costs nothing in stock.
cases.delivery_time_to_customer: About 5 to 9 business days after the customer approves the art (reports/scout-2026-11-13.md). Printful takes 2 to 5 business days to make an item, then 3 to 4 business days for US standard shipping, or 1 to 3 for express (https://www.printful.com/shipping, read Nov 21). Add up to a day for the proof (ASSUMED). Blanket and canvas ship as two parcels. Printful calls these estimates, not guarantees. This misses the house rule of 2 to 8 business days at the slow end, so the page must state the real time. Christmas cutoff for 2026: UNKNOWN. Printful's page (https://www.printful.com/holiday-order-deadlines) has a 2026 table I could not read. In 2025 the US cutoff was Dec 11 standard and Dec 16 express (https://www.printful.com/blog/your-holiday-shipping-and-order-deadline-guide).
strongest_evidence: Dhruv already approved this exact test. reports/decisions.md, Nov 18: 'Fast lane plus a print-on-demand dog-gift test (custom portrait blanket and canvas, made and shipped by a US print partner per order)', approved: B. CLAUDE.md also lists US print-on-demand as an allowed test-before-stock route.

The repo's own script shows money per order: $57.69 before ads, +$19.18 after benchmark ads, +$7.63 in the tough case (data/economics_outputs.csv, pet-portrait-bundle base). The best dropship product in ranked.md earns $0.21 in its tough case, and 14 of 16 lose money there.

Demand is proven, at lower prices. Crown & Paw has 20,199 Trustpilot reviews and West & Willow about 19,380. People pay $50 to $110 for illustrated pet art, and both sell it on blankets (research/sales-check-2026-11-13/top3-sales-evidence.json).

Costs are public and were rechecked today. Printful catalog: sherpa 50x60 $35.76, canvas 8x10 $15.81 (data/economics_inputs.csv, Nov 13). Shipping: sherpa $13.99, small canvas $6.79, plus a $0.40 US surcharge to Jan 17, 2027 (https://www.printful.com/shipping, read Nov 21). These are still ESTIMATED until a real order.

It is the most automatable model for a software person. Printful's API creates and confirms orders, makes mockups, quotes shipping, and sends webhooks for shipped, failed and on-hold orders, at 120 calls a minute (https://developers.printful.com/docs/). Printful replaces damaged or mislabeled items reported within 30 days (https://www.printful.com/blog/top-5-printful-policies-your-store-should-copy).
honest_weaknesses: The $149 price is unproven. Incumbents sell blanket plus canvas for about $100 before standing 20 to 25% codes (sales-check and data/economics_inputs.csv). reports/status-2026-11-15.md says HOLD, price unproven. In the low case each order loses $26.59. No script run exists for a $79 to $99 version, so that fallback is UNKNOWN.

It is slow for a fast lane and the window is short. Made to order: 5 to 9 business days after art approval, in two parcels. The sample will not arrive for about a week, so first ads would use mockups, not real sample photos. With a 2025 cutoff of Dec 11, there are about two weeks to sell, in the most expensive ad weeks of the year. After December, gift searches fall 70 to 90% (reports/scout-2026-11-13.md).

It breaks one of Dhruv's own terms. This market has large incumbents: Crown & Paw claims 850,000+ customers and West & Willow claims 1M+ portraits. Our only edge is better art and a fast preview, and the instant preview tool is not built. This week it would be a manual proof by email.

Personalized goods cannot be returned to stock. Printful does not refund buyer's remorse, and if Dhruv refunds anyway he pays the printing and shipping (Printful blog, Feb 26, 2025). Every order also needs a portrait made and checked by hand, inside 1 to 3 hours a day. The 5% refund rate and $5 art cost are ASSUMED.

The path to $10,000 a month is the weakest of the criteria. It needs about 520 orders a month at $19.18 (rough ASSUMED), Printful's unit cost does not fall with volume, and the Etsy route is slow: Printify says 165 days on average to the first $1,000 (vendor figure). Etsy fees in the repo are ESTIMATED (6.5% plus 3% and $0.25, and 15% on Offsite Ads orders; data/channel_params.json).
cases.path_to_10k_month: About 520 orders a month at the base $19.18 an order (rough ASSUMED), about 220 if the high case's $45.84 held. Requires $149 to convert at benchmark ad cost, demand beyond December (memorial, Mother's Day), and cheaper printing at volume. None of that is proven yet.
cases.automation_fit: Claude can automate: portrait art from the customer's photo, proof emails, mockups, Printful orders by API, tracking and delay notices, new design tests. Manual: Dhruv checks each portrait, approves ads and spend, applies store changes, answers complaints, reviews the sample.

cases.name: High-ticket dealer dropshipping from US brands
cases.model: High-ticket dealer dropshipping from US brands
cases.one_line: Best profit per order on paper in the repo, but it needs supplier approval, more cash and a rule change, so prepare it now and start it later.
how_it_works_steps: Dhruv decides whether to lift the 'no reselling another brand as the hero' rule for this lane. He picks one parcel-shipped niche (electric fireplaces first) and gets a domain email, a business phone and a Florida resale certificate (Form DR-1, free).

Build a finished niche store on Shopify with real category pages, policies and a phone number. Suppliers reject empty or 'coming soon' sites (research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/system_and_mechanics.md section 2).
Claude drafts dealer applications to many brands. Dhruv sends them. About 10 to 20% say yes, in 2 business days to 4 weeks (same file, self-reported by practitioners).
List approved products at the brand's MAP price. Run Google Shopping and search ads. Answer buyer questions by phone and chat.
The customer pays the store. Dhruv pays the supplier by card at order time. The supplier ships direct from US stock under the brand's warranty.
Shopify pays out (first payout about 7 to 14 days for a new store, battle_brief.md, ESTIMATED). Profit is what is left after product, dropship fee, card fee, refunds and ads.
cases.days_to_first_sale: About 6 weeks to 6 months. A first sale this week is not realistic. Fastest practitioner report: about a month to build the store, first sale about two weeks later (Jayden Clark, self-reported). A course seller says first sales in months 3 to 6 (Fenner). Main reason: no brand has approved Dhruv yet. Approval takes 2 business days to 4 weeks, about 10 to 20% of applications succeed, and buyers of $1,000+ items take 7 to 30 days to decide. Source: research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/system_and_mechanics.md sections 2, 4 and 6. Rough ASSUMED best case for Dhruv, who already has the LLC and can build a store fast with Claude: 3 to 5 weeks. That lands at the tail of the fireplace season, not the start.
cases.cash_needed_to_start: $912 for pizza ovens, $1,700 for electric fireplaces (research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/rank_outputs.json: $300 setup, plus paying the supplier for 1 order before payout, plus ads for 2 sales). The $300 setup is ASSUMED (rank_inputs.json: Shopify $1 intro, domain, business phone, logo, first month of apps; it excludes the liability insurance some suppliers ask for). Course seller Fenner says $3,000 to $10,000 to launch properly, and $1,000 to $2,000 is possible but slower (system_and_mechanics.md section 6). Only pizza ovens fit Dhruv's $500 to $1,000. Preparing now, without ads or orders, costs only the setup line.
cases.profit_per_order: On paper only. Nothing here is VERIFIED. Electric fireplace at an ASSUMED $1,500 price: $346.20 before ads, $175.00 ad cost, +$171.20 profit, +$118.70 in the tough case. Pizza oven at an ASSUMED $600 price: $129.30 before ads, $95.83 ad cost, +$33.47 profit, +$4.72 in the tough case. Source: research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/rank_outputs.json. These rest on a 30% dealer margin taken from dated 2014 hearth data, an ASSUMED conversion rate (0.8% and 1.2%) and head-keyword CPCs of $1.40 and $1.15 (DataForSEO). Real dealer discounts and real Shopping CPCs are UNKNOWN until a brand sends a price sheet and ads run. For comparison, the best fast-test product earns +$0.21 per order in the tough case (research/fast-test-2026-11-21/ranked.md).
cases.week1_sales_realistic: $0, zero orders. No application has been sent and no brand has approved Dhruv, so there is nothing he may list as an authorized dealer. The fastest supplier decision cited is 2 business days, and that is after a finished store exists. Buyers at this price take 7 to 30 days to decide (system_and_mechanics.md sections 2 and 4). His $500 to $1,000 does not cover the $1,700 start for fireplaces (rank_outputs.json). The appeal is real: one or two fireplace orders at the ASSUMED $1,500 price would pass the $2,000 stretch goal. But not next week. Honest role: a later second lane. This week, at most, Dhruv decides the rule question and Claude drafts dealer applications for fireplace brands (drafted, not sent).
cases.inventory_needed_up_front: None. The supplier holds the stock and ships each order. But every order is paid to the supplier by card before Shopify pays out: about $1,050 per fireplace order or $420 per pizza oven order (rank_outputs.json product lines, ESTIMATED at a 30% margin). Some brands ask for an opening order or a yearly minimum (about $10,000 for massage chairs; VEVOR asks about a $5,000 plus yearly budget; Fenner, course seller, system_and_mechanics.md sections 2 and 3). Those brands should be skipped. Dhruv's 'order one unit to himself' rule would cost one such supplier payment, which is most or all of his budget.
cases.delivery_time_to_customer: UNKNOWN until a dealer agreement and a test order. No brand's dealer ship time is in the repo. What is known: stock is in the US. Electric fireplaces and pizza ovens ship by parcel. Saunas ship by LTL freight with curbside delivery (research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/niches.md; system_and_mechanics.md section 5). Under the FTC rule we could state only a time the supplier confirms.
strongest_evidence: Profit per order has real room on paper. Electric fireplaces: +$171.20 at benchmark ad cost and +$118.70 in the tough case (research/high-ticket-2026-11-19/rank_outputs.json, ASSUMED and ESTIMATED inputs). The best of 16 fast-test products earns +$0.21 in the tough case, and none pass the cushion rule (research/fast-test-2026-11-21/ranked.md).
The path to $10,000 a month needs far fewer orders: 59 fireplace orders a month (rank_outputs.json, orders_per_month_10k) against about 295 for Barkfare (battle_brief.md).

Demand is proven and in season. 'Electric fireplace' has 135,000 US searches a month at a $1.40 CPC, with a Dec/Jan index of 1.67, the strongest of 17 niches (niches.md, DataForSEO, checked 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-19). Buyers search for the product, so the model does not depend on video ads, creators or Dhruv on camera (channel per system_and_mechanics.md section 4).

It matches his shipping and trust wishes by design: real US brands, US stock, parcel shipping, mostly 120V plug-in units, and a warranty tied to authorized dealers (niches.md). The brief found generic products with slow delivery score 1.4 to 3.3 on Trustpilot (battle_brief.md).

Of 24 options scored for a $2,000 start, electric fireplaces rank 2nd (54) and pizza ovens 3rd (53), behind Barkfare at 72 (rank_outputs.json; reports/full-synopsis-2026-11-19.md section 10). Much of the setup overlaps with Barkfare: the LLC exists and liability insurance is already required (system_and_mechanics.md section 8).
honest_weaknesses: It cannot produce a sale this week. No dealer approval exists. Approval takes 2 business days to 4 weeks, about 10 to 20% of applications succeed, and first sales are reported at about 6 weeks to 6 months (system_and_mechanics.md sections 2 and 6). Sending applications also needs Dhruv's approval. This fails his speed test outright.

It needs more cash than the lane allows. Fireplaces need $1,700 to start against his $500 to $1,000 (rank_outputs.json). One supplier payment of about $1,050 goes out before any payout, and Shopify can hold a reserve, for example 10% for 120 days.
